steps.intent: Algeria’s objectives are to secure an immediate ceasefire and full implementation of resolution 2735, restore humanitarian access, protect civilians and aid seekers, and block any forced displacement or territorial change in Gaza. The main difficulties will be the United States, which is likely to resist language on ceasefire, accountability and settlements, and balancing that with explicit condemnation of the 7 October attacks and hostage-taking to avoid a veto. Keeping the E10 co-sponsors unified while retaining strong language on humanitarian access and two-State parameters will also require careful negotiation.

messages.China: China supports the draft as a basis and appreciates Algeria’s leadership. We ask that OP1 explicitly demand an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire and cessation of all military operations, and that OP4 require an end to the blockade and the opening of all crossings with UNRWA’s central role protected. OP7 should expressly reject any forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza, including to third countries, and OP3 should include diplomatic personnel among those protected. We are ready to work with the penholder to finalize a text that can be adopted without delay.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft and thanks Algeria for its work. We ask that OP1 explicitly call upon Hamas to accept and implement the ceasefire proposal without delay and without condition, mirroring resolution 2735 (2024), so that the demand for a ceasefire is clearly tied to hostage release. We also suggest adding follow-up reporting every 60 days in OP11. Denmark remains firmly committed to humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and the two-State solution.
messages.France: France supports the draft’s core objective: an immediate and permanent ceasefire, unimpeded humanitarian access, release of all hostages, rejection of displacement and a path to the two-State solution. To strengthen Council unity and balance, we ask the penholder to name Hamas in the condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks, to add an explicit reference to Israel’s security and security guarantees, and to ensure humanitarian access is channelled through UN mechanisms and UNRWA. These changes would allow France to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft and is pleased to co-sponsor it. To strengthen consensus and reflect our consistent position, we ask that the text explicitly name Hamas in the condemnation of 7 October and in the hostage-release demand, and that it reaffirm the right of self-defence in accordance with international law. These changes would make the text more balanced without weakening its humanitarian core.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a co-sponsor and thanks Algeria for its leadership. We request that OP1 expressly include a permanent ceasefire, consistent with resolution 2735's second phase, and that OP5 name UNRWA and its central role in the humanitarian response. These are important to Guyana and would strengthen the text without altering its balanced framework.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan co-sponsored this draft and supports its prompt adoption. We ask that OP4 expressly require lifting the unlawful blockade and that OP5 name UNRWA and call for predictable funding. We also seek stronger OP8 language demanding that Israel, the occupying Power, cease and rescind settlement decisions.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as a co-sponsor and believes it offers an urgent, balanced response to the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza while reaffirming resolution 2735 (2024), the release of all hostages, and the two-State solution. Panama does not request changes at this stage and urges the Council to preserve unity and move to adoption without delay.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current draft as a co-sponsor and believes it reflects the Council’s long-standing calls for an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access and a political horizon based on the two-State solution. We urge all Council members to preserve unity and adopt the text without weakening its core operational demands. We remain ready to engage constructively on any technical refinements, but we do not see a need to reopen substantive elements at this stage.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the aim of ending the bloodshed and addressing the humanitarian catastrophe, but the draft cannot make an unconditional ceasefire conditional on implementation of resolution 2735 (2024), on which we abstained. We therefore insist on clear language demanding an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, on lifting the blockade, and on preserving UNRWA's mandate. We are ready to work constructively, but these points are fundamental.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks Algeria for coordinating this draft and confirms its support as a co-sponsor. We believe the text is strong and balanced, but we request two refinements: explicit protection for diplomatic personnel and United Nations personnel in OP3, reflecting the recent reported incident involving a diplomatic delegation, and strengthened accountability reporting in OP11. These changes are consistent with our consistent emphasis on protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel and accountability under international law.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports this draft, which we are co-sponsoring, and asks for its swift adoption. We would like the text to expressly protect UNRWA’s mandate and access, to affirm voluntary and dignified return, and to recall the binding nature of the International Court of Justice’s provisional measures. These changes strengthen the Council’s consistency with international law and the humanitarian imperative in Gaza.
messages.Somalia: Somalia remains a co-sponsor of this draft and supports its core demands for an immediate ceasefire, release of all hostages, unimpeded humanitarian access and protection of civilians. We ask that OP5 explicitly recognize UNRWA's essential role and ensure its ability to continue its mandate and operations in Gaza. This addition would strengthen the humanitarian response without altering the balance of the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the objective of this draft: an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, a major scaling-up of humanitarian aid and a pathway to a two-State solution. To enable the broadest possible support, we ask the penholder to name Hamas clearly in the condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks and to call on Hamas to accept and implement the ceasefire proposal without delay or condition. We also believe the text should reaffirm Israel's right to self-defence in accordance with international law, alongside the security of all States in the region.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support the current draft. It fails to make clear that Hamas must accept the ceasefire proposal and release all hostages, and it contains language on displacement and settlements that prejudges final-status issues and contradicts our policy. We will veto this text unless these red lines are addressed.

replies.Panama: accepted: no changes requested; core text preserved.

replies.Russian Federation: accepted: OP1 no longer conditions ceasefire on 2735 implementation and demands immediate unconditional permanent ceasefire; blockade and UNRWA language included.

steps.summary: The revision retains Algeria’s core objectives on an immediate permanent ceasefire, humanitarian access, UNRWA and protection of Palestinians while incorporating enough Hamas, hostage-release and Israeli security language to avoid a United States veto. The United States is expected to abstain rather than block; all other Council members are expected to vote in favour.

messages.China: China supports the revised draft and appreciates the incorporation of key amendments. We still believe the Council must explicitly reject any plan or action to forcibly displace Palestinian civilians from Gaza to third countries, especially given recent public statements; recalling paragraph 5 of resolution 2735 is necessary but not sufficient. China will support the text if this language is reflected as a new operative paragraph after OP10.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current text as a balanced and operational basis for Council action. We welcome the incorporation of our previous requests in OP1 and OP12, in particular the call on Hamas to accept and implement the ceasefire proposal and the regular reporting cycle. Denmark will vote in favour and urges all Council members to preserve unity behind the resolution.
messages.France: France supports the current text and will vote in favour if it is put to the vote. We thank the penholder for incorporating our priorities, in particular the explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks, Israel's security and self-defence, support for UNRWA and humanitarian principles, and the categories of hostages. Given the catastrophic situation in Gaza, the Council must speak with one voice and act without further delay; we call on all members to support this draft.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous concerns: Hamas is clearly named, hostage release is demanded of Hamas and all parties, and the right of self-defence is reaffirmed. We support the current balanced text and have no further changes to request; we urge the Council to proceed to a vote without delay.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for incorporating its earlier requests, in particular the permanent ceasefire language in OP1 and the explicit reference to UNRWA in the humanitarian response provisions. We support the revised text as it stands and urge all Council members to rally behind it to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and to advance a sustainable ceasefire and the two-State solution.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft as a co-sponsor and welcomes the inclusion of blockade lifting and UNRWA funding. We still seek explicit operational language rejecting forcible displacement and demographic change in Gaza, and at least an express reference to settlement activities in OP9. We also ask that the blockade be described as unlawful, consistent with international law; these changes are necessary for the text to reflect the Council’s obligations and the reality in Gaza.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft as a co-sponsor and believes it reflects the Council’s responsibility to demand an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and unhindered humanitarian access. We urge all members to preserve the text’s balance and adopt it without further delay so that the Council can speak with one voice on the catastrophic situation in Gaza and on the two-State solution.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised draft and remains a co-sponsor. We welcome that it preserves the core operational demands: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, full humanitarian access, protection of civilians and UN personnel, and reaffirmation of the two-State solution. We urge all Council members to unite behind the text so that it can have a tangible impact on the ground.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the revised draft as a basis and welcomes the acceptance of our key amendments on an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire and on lifting the blockade. We still need the text to be balanced and free of loopholes: obligations must apply to all parties, humanitarian access cannot be made subject to vague security caveats, and the Council must explicitly demand an end to settlement activity. We ask the penholder to reflect these points in the final text so that we can support it.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised text as drafted and welcomes the incorporation of its earlier requests on the protection of diplomatic and United Nations personnel in OP4 and strengthened accountability reporting in OP12. As a co-sponsor, we urge Council members to preserve unity and adopt the text without further delay so that the Council can respond to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. Sierra Leone remains committed to an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access, and the two-State solution.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised text and thanks Algeria and the E10 for incorporating our earlier requests on UNRWA access and mandate, voluntary and dignified return, and compliance with ICJ provisional measures. The text provides a firm and balanced Council response to the catastrophic situation in Gaza and should be put to the vote without delay. We urge all Council members to support it and call on all parties to implement its provisions fully and immediately.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating its proposed language on UNRWA in OP5 and OP6. We support the current text as a balanced and urgent basis for Council action and call for its swift adoption without further amendments. We urge all members to unite behind an immediate ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, and we call on all parties to comply with the resolution and international law.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current text as a balanced and urgent response to the catastrophic situation in Gaza. We welcome the clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the call on Hamas to accept and implement the ceasefire proposal, and the reaffirmation of Israel’s right to self-defence alongside the right of all States in the region to live in peace and security. The United Kingdom will vote in favour and urges all Council members to unite behind this resolution.
messages.United States of America: The United States appreciates the penholder's efforts and the strengthened condemnation of Hamas and hostage release language. However, the current text still demands an unconditional ceasefire not conditioned on the release of all hostages, retains blocking language on UNRWA and 'ending the blockade,' and references the ICJ's provisional measures. Unless these red lines are addressed, the United States cannot support the text and will oppose it.

replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP5 and OP9 incorporated; OP1 reflects a compromise retaining the call on Hamas while adding parallel release and all-party implementation
replies.United States of America: rejected: the red lines would condition the ceasefire on hostage release, remove blockade, UNRWA and ICJ provisions, and weaken condemnation of attacks on civilians, contrary to Algeria’s long-standing position

steps.summary: The revision incorporates China, Pakistan and Russia while preserving the core demands for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, lifting the unlawful blockade, support for UNRWA, rejection of forcible displacement and demographic change, and accountability including ICJ provisional measures. It is expected to attract broad support but face a United States veto.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria is the penholder and sponsor of the draft, and its established policy strongly supports an immediate ceasefire, humanitarian access, rejection of displacement, and accountability. It would vote yes and speak before the vote to urge adoption and highlight the humanitarian imperative.
reasons.China: China supported prior ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions and its requested explicit rejection of forcible displacement was accepted. Voting in favour aligns with its record, while a pre-vote explanation underscores the urgency and its longstanding positions on Gaza, UNRWA, settlements and the two-State solution.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark is a listed co-sponsor and supported the draft in the last negotiation round, consistent with its emphasis on humanitarian law, hostages, UNRWA, and the two-State solution. It would vote yes even if a veto by another member is expected.
reasons.France: France has consistently voted in favour of ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions on Gaza, including the 14-1-0 draft vetoed in November 2024. Its established position supports this text’s core demands—ceasefire, hostages, humanitarian access, rejection of forced displacement, and two-State solution—so it would vote yes and explain its vote before the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece co-sponsored the draft and supported it in the last negotiation round, reflecting its strong priority on humanitarian access, civilian protection, release of hostages and a two-State solution. Voting in favour is consistent with its Council record and elected-member role.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana is a co-sponsor of this draft and has consistently supported immediate ceasefire, humanitarian access, hostage release, UNRWA, and the two-State solution, including voting in favour of similar prior texts. Its vote is therefore yes.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan co-sponsored the draft and its requested amendments were accepted, so it would vote in favour and explain its support for a ceasefire, humanitarian access, rejection of displacement and two-State solution.
reasons.Panama: Panama is a co-sponsor of the draft and supported it in the final negotiation round without requests; voting yes is consistent with its support for a ceasefire, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea co-sponsored the draft and consistently supported immediate ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, and two-State language in prior votes. As an elected member and co-sponsor, it would vote yes and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently backed immediate ceasefire drafts and Palestinian humanitarian and political demands; despite partial acceptance of its amendments, the final text serves its core objectives and is likely to be supported.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone co-sponsored this draft and has consistently voted for ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions on Gaza, so it would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote. The text aligns closely with its stated positions on civilian protection, hostages, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia co-sponsored the draft, requested no changes in the last round, and has consistently voted for ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions on Gaza. Voting in favour with a pre-vote explanation matches its co-sponsorship and established foreign policy.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia is a co-sponsor and the draft aligns with its support for a ceasefire, humanitarian access, Palestinian rights, and a two-State solution. Voting in favour is consistent with its position in the last negotiation round.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom was recorded as supporting the draft in the final negotiation round and has consistently backed Security Council action demanding a ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, and a two-State solution. It would therefore vote in favour, and as a supporting non-sponsor it is unlikely to request the floor for a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.United States of America: The draft rejects the US red lines on conditioning a ceasefire on hostage release and on removing blockade, UNRWA, and ICJ language, so the United States would veto it. A pre-vote explanation is consistent with US practice and its stated position.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council, which we have submitted together with partners because the situation in Gaza demands that this Council finally act. The text is not a perfect text, but it responds to the bare minimum required by humanity: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, the lifting of the unlawful blockade, unimpeded humanitarian access at scale, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, rejection of forced displacement, and accountability for violations of international law. We call on all members to uphold their responsibilities and not allow this Council to remain silent while Palestinian lives continue to be lost. Algeria will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their legitimate national rights, including their right to self-determination and an independent State, and we urge the Council to adopt this resolution without delay.
before.China: China will vote in favour of this draft resolution. For more than 18 months, the Security Council has been unable to meet the expectations of the international community, while Gaza has suffered an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. The draft before us reflects the overwhelming consensus of the international community: an immediate, unconditional and lasting ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the exchange of prisoners; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access to all parts of Gaza, including the north; the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; and the full implementation of the two-State solution. China supports these demands. We welcome the inclusion of clear language rejecting any plan or action to forcibly displace Palestinian civilians from Gaza to third countries. Any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza is unacceptable. We also condemn the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all violence against civilians. We call on all parties, especially Israel, to implement this resolution without delay, lift the blockade and open all crossings, respect UNRWA’s mandate, cease settlement activities and refrain from actions that undermine the two-State solution. The Security Council must not remain silent in the face of continuing death and destruction. China will continue to stand with the people of Gaza and with the just cause of the Palestinian people.
before.Denmark: Denmark is a co-sponsor of this draft resolution and will vote in favour. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands urgent action by this Council. Denmark has unequivocally condemned the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October, and we reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, the killing and injury of civilians, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, attacks on schools, hospitals, shelters, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises, and the obstruction of humanitarian relief are unacceptable. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza. Denmark supports the essential role of UNRWA and other humanitarian agencies and calls for adequate and predictable funding. We reject any demographic or territorial change in Gaza and any forced displacement of Palestinian civilians. The only sustainable path remains a negotiated two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Denmark calls on all parties to implement this resolution in good faith and on the Council to remain seized of the matter, including with regard to accountability for violations.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. The Security Council must not remain silent in the face of continued civilian suffering, the destruction of essential infrastructure, restrictions on humanitarian access, and the risk of famine. France has consistently called for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the protection of civilians, full respect for international humanitarian law, and humanitarian access at scale for all Palestinians in need. This text also condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and hostage-taking, while recalling the right of all States in the region, including Israel, to live in peace and security within secure and recognised borders. France fully rejects any forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza and any attempt at demographic or territorial change. The only viable path is the two-State solution, with a viable, independent and contiguous Palestinian State, and Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. France calls on all members of this Council to support this resolution. The Council’s unity is indispensable if we are to make a difference on the ground.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this resolution, which it is proud to co-sponsor. The catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza requires an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel, medical personnel, journalists and United Nations premises. Greece condemns the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all attacks against civilians. We reaffirm our unwavering support for the two-State solution and for the unity of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority, and we call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and to implement this resolution without delay.
before.Guyana:
Thank you. Guyana has the honour to speak in favour of the draft resolution before the Council and to have joined its co-sponsorship. The situation in Gaza demands that this Council not remain silent in the face of catastrophic civilian suffering, the continued holding of hostages, the collapse of essential services and repeated attacks affecting schools, shelters, hospitals, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises.

The text before us responds to the most urgent imperatives: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale, including through UNRWA; respect for international humanitarian law; accountability; and a clear rejection of any demographic or territorial change or forcible displacement in Gaza. It also upholds the two-State solution and the centrality of Gaza as part of the Palestinian territory occupied in 1967, unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

Guyana therefore votes in favour. We urge all members to support this resolution and to ensure that the Council’s voice is translated into compliance, protection and relief for civilians, Israelis and Palestinians alike, and a credible path back to a just and lasting peace.
before.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. As a co-sponsor, Pakistan believes that the Council cannot remain silent in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the continuing loss of civilian lives, the destruction of hospitals, schools, shelters and United Nations premises, and the deepening suffering of the Palestinian people.

The resolution is balanced and firm: it demands an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; full respect for international humanitarian law; unhindered humanitarian access at scale, including through UNRWA; the lifting of the unlawful blockade; and accountability for all violations. It also rejects any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including forcible displacement, and reaffirms the two-State solution and the unity of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

Pakistan unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all attacks against civilians, including by Israeli forces. We support the diplomatic efforts of Egypt, Qatar and the United States, and we call for compliance with the provisional measures of the International Court of Justice.

The Council has a Charter responsibility to act. Pakistan will therefore vote in favour and urges all members to do the same, so that the Council can finally speak with one voice to stop the bloodshed and create a credible path towards a just, lasting and comprehensive peace, including the realization of the independent State of Palestine.
before.Panama: Panama votes in favour of this resolution. As a co-sponsor, we believe the Security Council must speak clearly against the catastrophic humanitarian situation, demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, call for an immediate ceasefire and full humanitarian access, and reaffirm the two-State solution. Panama remains committed to international law, the protection of civilians, and the authority of this Council.
before.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. As a co-sponsor, we believe the Council must speak clearly at this critical moment: there must be an immediate ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and full respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians, including humanitarian and United Nations personnel.

The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands urgent action. We strongly condemn the Hamas terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking, and we also stress that the suffering of Palestinian civilians cannot continue. The Council must reject any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza and must preserve the prospect of a two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

The Republic of Korea appreciates the mediation efforts of Egypt, Qatar and the United States, and we urge all parties to return to diplomacy in good faith. We call on all Council members to act with unity and responsibility so that this resolution can translate into tangible protection for civilians and relief for those in desperate need.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Algeria and the co-sponsors for their intensive work and for their readiness to take into account the concerns of Council members. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires the Council to act without further delay. This text demands an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access, the lifting of the blockade and the protection of civilians. It rejects any attempt at demographic or territorial change, including the forcible displacement of Palestinians, and it rightly calls for an end to settlement activity and respect for the two-State solution. The draft is not ideal, and not all of our proposals were fully reflected, but the central provisions are balanced and respond to the overwhelming demand of the international community. We call on all members of the Council to support this resolution and not to block the Council’s voice at this critical moment.
before.Sierra Leone:
Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone is a co-sponsor of this draft resolution and will vote in favour of it. We do so because the catastrophic situation in Gaza requires urgent and decisive action by this Council. The continued loss of civilian life, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, the obstruction of humanitarian relief, and the repeated attacks on civilians, humanitarian personnel, United Nations premises and diplomatic personnel are unacceptable, and prior resolutions must be implemented in full.

This draft reflects elements that Sierra Leone has consistently supported: an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, rejection of any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and a renewed commitment to the two-State solution. Sierra Leone calls on all parties to comply with their obligations under international law and to engage in good faith with diplomatic efforts. We urge all members of this Council to support this text and to act with the unity and urgency that the situation demands.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us, which we are proud to have co-sponsored. The catastrophic situation in Gaza requires this Council to act with urgency, unity and clarity. We call for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale throughout the Gaza Strip. All parties must respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians and civilian objects, including schools, hospitals, shelters, humanitarian and United Nations personnel, medical personnel, journalists and diplomatic personnel. UNRWA’s mandate and operations must be supported and protected. There must be no forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza, no demographic or territorial change, and no reduction of Gaza’s territory. The only sustainable path remains a two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Slovenia supports this resolution because it demands action, upholds international law and ensures that the Security Council remains seized of this matter.
before.Somalia: Mr President, Somalia takes the floor in support of the draft resolution before the Council, which we are honoured to co-sponsor. The situation in Gaza demands urgent Council action: an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access at scale, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and accountability for violations of international humanitarian law. Somalia reiterates its firm support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including self-determination, and for a two-State solution with an independent and sovereign Palestine living side by side with Israel in peace and security within recognized borders. We condemn all attacks against civilians, including terrorism and hostage-taking, and stress that the Gaza Strip must remain an integral part of the Palestinian territory, with no demographic or territorial change. Somalia calls on all parties to comply with this resolution without delay and on all Council members to support it.
before.United States of America: The United States regrets that the Council is being asked to vote on a deeply unbalanced draft that would not advance the release of hostages or a durable ceasefire. We engaged in good faith and made clear the essential elements of any credible text: the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, including American citizens; a ceasefire that is conditioned upon and accompanied by that release; expanded humanitarian access through all available crossings while respecting Israel’s legitimate security needs; and language that does not reward Hamas’s refusal to negotiate or tie Israel’s hands in defending its people. The penholder rejected those necessary changes. Instead, this draft demands an unconditional ceasefire without ensuring the release of hostages, fails to squarely confront Hamas’s continued hostage-taking, calls for lifting the blockade without adequate security arrangements, and includes provisions that would undermine the impartiality of United Nations humanitarian mechanisms and politicize the Council’s work. The United States remains committed to delivering life-saving assistance to Palestinians in Gaza and to a durable peace in which Israelis and Palestinians can live in safety. But we cannot support a text that does not secure the hostages and does not advance the cause of peace. For that reason, the United States will vote against this draft resolution.

after.Algeria:
Mr President,

Algeria takes the floor after this vote with deep regret and profound anger. The draft resolution submitted by Algeria and co-sponsored by fourteen members of this Council was not adopted because of the negative vote of one permanent member, the United States of America. Fourteen members voted in favour. Fourteen members heard the cries of Gaza. Fourteen members chose humanity, international law and the will of the international community. One member chose to shield the occupying Power.

This veto does not wipe away the demands contained in the text. It does not erase the fact that an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire is a moral and legal imperative. It does not erase the obligation to release all hostages immediately and unconditionally. It does not erase the obligation to lift the unlawful blockade and allow safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale to all parts of Gaza. It does not erase the prohibition of forced displacement, demographic change and territorial change. It does not erase the reality that Palestinian lives matter.

Algeria has said before, and says again today: the Security Council cannot continue to be held hostage by a veto while Palestinian civilians are killed, starved, displaced and denied medical care. The Israeli occupying forces continue their massacres, including strikes on schools, shelters, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is man-made. It is the result of a brutal blockade, continued military operations and the impunity granted to the occupying Power. The latest attacks near aid distribution centres, the killing of civilians seeking food, the expansion of settlements in the occupied West Bank, and the attacks on diplomatic personnel must be condemned and investigated. There must be accountability.

Algeria voted in favour of this draft because it represented the bare minimum that this Council should have adopted: ceasefire, release of hostages, humanitarian access, protection of civilians, rejection of forced displacement, and a horizon of two-State solution with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We thank all members who voted in favour and all co-sponsors who stood with justice. We especially note that the United Kingdom joined the overwhelming majority. The isolation of the United States in this Chamber is clear.

But let no one believe that this veto ends the matter. Algeria will not remain silent. We will continue to act in the Security Council, in the General Assembly and in all relevant international fora. We will continue to demand the implementation of resolution 2735 and all relevant resolutions. We will continue to call for Chapter VII action, for accountability and for sanctions against those who defy the collective will of this Council. We will continue to stand with the Palestinian people in their legitimate struggle for self-determination, freedom and justice, and for an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian State, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The blood of the martyrs in Gaza is not forgotten. The mothers burying their children are not forgotten. The hungry, the wounded and the displaced are not forgotten. Algeria will not forget. And this Council, and those who vetoed today, will be judged by history.

Thank you.
after.China:
Thank you, Mr. President. China voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that it was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The result — 14 members in favour and one against — clearly shows where the overwhelming majority of the Council and the international community stand. The draft was not a perfect text, but it reflected the minimum demands of humanity and of this Council’s own prior resolutions: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and arbitrarily detained persons; the exchange of Palestinian prisoners; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas in Gaza; safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza; the protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel, medical personnel, journalists and United Nations personnel; and accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law.

China is deeply disappointed that the Council has again been prevented from speaking with one voice at a moment when Gaza continues to endure an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. The United States’ veto cannot erase the facts on the ground, nor can it absolve the Council of its responsibilities. It has dashed the hopes of the Palestinian people, deepened their suffering and further undermined the authority and credibility of the Security Council. Every veto cast in the face of continued civilian deaths will be recorded and judged by history.

China reiterates its firm opposition to any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including the forcible displacement of Palestinians. Gaza must be unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. The two-State solution remains the only viable way forward: two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders consistent with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions.

China condemns all attacks against civilians, including the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023, and all acts of hostage-taking. At the same time, the suffering of Palestinian civilians cannot continue. Israel must comply with its obligations under international humanitarian law, lift restrictions on humanitarian access and cease attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. All parties must immediately implement a ceasefire and create conditions for lasting peace.

China calls on the parties concerned to respond to the overwhelming consensus of the international community, and on all members of the Council not to relent in their efforts. China will continue to stand with the Palestinian people in their legitimate national rights and to work for an immediate ceasefire, humanitarian relief, justice and a comprehensive, just and lasting solution.
after.Denmark:
Mr President,

Denmark regrets that this Council has again been unable to adopt a resolution on Gaza. We voted in favour and were proud to co-sponsor the text because the humanitarian catastrophe demands an immediate and lasting ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and respect for international humanitarian law by all parties.

The failure to act does not diminish the obligations on the parties. Denmark again condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks of 7 October and all hostage-taking. We continue to demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, the killing of civilians, attacks on schools, hospitals, shelters, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises, and the obstruction of relief are unacceptable. Israel must comply with international humanitarian law, including proportionality and precaution, and facilitate safe and unhindered aid throughout Gaza. UNRWA and all humanitarian actors must be able to carry out their mandates.

Denmark remains committed to the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognised borders. The Council cannot remain silent or inactive. Denmark will continue to work with all members, including the United States, to ensure that this Council responds to the crisis, upholds resolution 2735 (2024), and contributes to a sustainable peace. The humanitarian situation in Gaza requires nothing less.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this draft resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted owing to the veto of a permanent member. At a time when the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic, when civilians continue to be killed, displaced and deprived of essential goods, and when the credibility of this Council is at stake, the Security Council could not send the clear message that the international community expects. France regrets this failure. A veto must not become a substitute for action when so many civilian lives are at risk.

France reiterates its demands with the utmost firmness: an immediate and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, including the two French hostages still held in Gaza; and full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale throughout the Gaza Strip. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, and refrain from attacks on schools, hospitals, shelters, humanitarian distribution points, United Nations premises and humanitarian personnel. The restrictions on humanitarian access and the obstruction of relief convoys are unacceptable and must end. UNRWA and all humanitarian actors must be able to carry out their mandate.

France continues to condemn unequivocally the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking. It also recalls that Israel has the right to live in security, within secure and recognised borders. But that right does not dispense with the obligations of international humanitarian law. France rejects any forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza, any demographic or territorial change, and any annexation. The Gaza Strip must be an integral part of a future Palestinian State and be unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

The only credible horizon remains the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security. France will not stop working to that end. It calls on the parties to return to negotiations, to implement resolution 2735 (2024) without delay, and to put the interests of civilians above all else. The Security Council cannot accept paralysis. France will continue to shoulder its responsibilities and to work with all members to overcome the current blockage and to respond to the emergency in Gaza.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council and was honoured to co-sponsor it. We deeply regret that, despite the support of 14 members, the draft has not been adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member.

The Council has again failed to meet its responsibilities at a moment of catastrophic human suffering in Gaza. The text before us was clear, balanced and grounded in international law and in the Council’s own prior decisions, including resolution 2735 (2024). It demanded an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale, including through UNRWA; protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; and respect for international humanitarian law. It condemned the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all attacks against civilians, rejected any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and reaffirmed the two-State solution.

Guyana regrets that the Council could not speak with one voice. A veto cannot erase the obligations of the parties under international law, nor the demands of the Charter, nor the urgency of the humanitarian crisis. The hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally. Civilians must be protected. Humanitarian relief must reach all those in need. Unilateral actions that undermine peace must cease.

Guyana will continue to support all serious efforts to secure a ceasefire, alleviate suffering and advance a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution, with two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders. The Security Council must not abandon its responsibility. Guyana remains seized of this matter and will continue to work with all members to that end.

Thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of this draft resolution as a co-sponsor because it reflected the minimum demanded by international law, human dignity and the overwhelming will of the international community: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; unimpeded humanitarian access at scale, including through UNRWA; the lifting of the unlawful blockade; the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; accountability for violations; and rejection of any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including forced displacement.

We deeply regret that, notwithstanding the support of fourteen members of this Council, this draft resolution has not been adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. Once again, the Security Council has been prevented from discharging its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security at a moment when Gaza is enduring an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe and when Palestinian civilians continue to be killed, displaced and deprived of the most basic means of survival.

Pakistan believes that the use or threat of the veto in the face of such grave and continuing violations cannot serve the cause of peace, justice or the credibility of this Council. It risks emboldening further violations of international humanitarian law and further eroding confidence in the multilateral system. The Security Council cannot remain silent while hospitals, schools, shelters, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises are attacked and while the Palestinian people face starvation, displacement and collective punishment.

Pakistan reaffirms its full solidarity with the Palestinian people and their legitimate, inalienable right to self-determination. A just and lasting peace in the Middle East requires an end to the Israeli occupation and the realization of the two-State solution, with an independent and sovereign State of Palestine on the basis of the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, living side by side with Israel in peace and security. Gaza must remain an integral part of the Palestinian State and must be unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Any attempt at forced displacement or demographic or territorial change in Gaza is unlawful and must be rejected.

We call for the immediate implementation of existing Security Council resolutions, for an end to the aggression against Gaza, for the unconditional release of all hostages, for the lifting of the blockade, and for safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access to all parts of Gaza. Pakistan will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and will continue to support every genuine effort to end their suffering and to achieve a just, comprehensive and lasting peace.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the draft resolution as a co-sponsor. We deeply regret that, despite the overwhelming support of 14 members of this Council, the draft was not adopted. At a time when civilians in Gaza continue to endure catastrophic suffering, the Council’s inability to act erodes its credibility and, more importantly, risks costing more lives.

We reiterate our strong condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups on 7 October 2023 and of all acts of hostage-taking. The immediate and unconditional release of all hostages remains imperative. At the same time, the killing and injury of Palestinian civilians, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, attacks on schools, shelters, hospitals, humanitarian distribution points and United Nations premises, and the obstruction of humanitarian relief are unacceptable. All parties must comply with international humanitarian law and protect civilians.

The Republic of Korea will continue to support an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; and a political horizon based on the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We reject any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza and any forced displacement of Palestinians.

Resolution 2735 (2024) remains in force and must be implemented in full. Today’s outcome should not mark the end of this Council’s efforts. We appreciate the continued mediation efforts of the United States, Egypt and Qatar, and we call on all members, especially the permanent members, to redouble diplomatic efforts, overcome divisions and ensure that the Council speaks with one voice to end the suffering and secure the release of all hostages. The Republic of Korea remains ready to work with all Council members to that end.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution because it reflected the central and urgent demands of the international community: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire in Gaza; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale; the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; and a clear rejection of any attempt at demographic or territorial change, including the forcible displacement of Palestinians. We thank Algeria and all co-sponsors for their work.

The result before the Council is sobering. Fourteen members voted in favour. Only one member, the United States of America, blocked the Council from adopting this text. Once again, the Security Council has been prevented from shouldering its Charter responsibility. Once again, we have heard the same explanations from the United States, which have no new substance. The American delegation claims that the text was unbalanced, but the only imbalance we see is the continued protection by Washington of Israeli military operations against the backdrop of an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza.

We note that it was the United States itself that sponsored resolution 2735, which welcomed a ceasefire proposal and rejected any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza. Today the United States has vetoed a draft that sought precisely to implement those commitments and to bring the bloodshed to an end. This is not a question of diplomacy; it is a question of political will and double standards.

The Russian Federation will not tire of demanding an immediate end to the violence, the release of all hostages, the lifting of the blockade, unimpeded humanitarian relief, and respect for international humanitarian law. The decisions of this Council must not remain paper. The suffering of the Palestinian people and the security of all civilians in the region require action, not obstruction. We will remain seized of the matter and will continue to support every genuine effort to stop the war and to advance the two-State solution.
after.Sierra Leone:
Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council and was proud to co-sponsor it. We deeply regret that the Council has again been unable to adopt a text that commanded the support of 14 of its 15 members. That outcome does not reflect a lack of consensus in this Chamber, but the exercise of a veto at a moment when Gaza demands that this Council act. Sierra Leone respects the procedures of the Security Council, but we cannot accept that procedural outcomes leave the Council unable to respond to catastrophic civilian suffering.

This draft was not a perfect text. No text could fully capture the pain, complexity and urgency of the situation. But it was balanced, and it was grounded in the Charter, in existing resolutions and in the most basic demands of humanity: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the exchange of Palestinian prisoners; the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas; safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale; the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel; and accountability for violations of international law. These are not optional requests. They are obligations.

Sierra Leone reiterates that all parties must respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and civilian objects, and ensure humanitarian access. The repeated attacks on schools, hospitals, shelters, aid distribution points and United Nations premises, and the obstruction of relief, are unacceptable. We condemn all attacks against civilians, including the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking. The hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally.

We also reaffirm our firm opposition to any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including forced displacement, and to any action that reduces the territory of Gaza. We support the unification of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority and the vision of a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognised borders.

The failure to adopt this resolution does not diminish the obligations of the parties, nor does it relieve the Security Council of its responsibility under the Charter. Sierra Leone calls on all members to redouble diplomatic efforts to secure a ceasefire, alleviate suffering and restore hope. The Council must remain seized of this matter. We will continue to support every effort to save lives and advance peace, dignity and justice for Palestinians and Israelis alike. Thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Thank you, Mr President.

Slovenia voted in favour of the draft resolution before this Council, which we co-sponsored, and we deeply regret that it has not been adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. Fourteen members of this Council spoke with one clear voice: the catastrophic situation in Gaza requires an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale; protection of civilians and civilian objects; and full respect for international humanitarian law and human rights law.

The rejection of this draft does not diminish the obligations of the parties under international law, nor does it diminish the responsibility of this Council to remain engaged. Slovenia will continue to insist on the implementation of relevant Council resolutions, including resolution 2735 (2024), and on the urgent need to end the suffering of civilians in Gaza, including through the protection of UNRWA’s mandate and operations. We reiterate our firm rejection of any forced displacement, any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and any unilateral action that undermines the two-State solution. The violence in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, must also end, and settlement expansion must cease. We call on all parties to prioritise the protection of civilian life and to return to negotiations in good faith. This Council must not be deterred from its duty to uphold international peace and security, and Slovenia will continue to work with all members towards a united and effective response.
after.Somalia: Mr President, Somalia voted in favour of the draft resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted. The Council’s failure to act must not become a licence for continued suffering. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains catastrophic; civilians, humanitarian workers, medical personnel and United Nations premises must be protected; all hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally; and safe, unhindered humanitarian access at scale must be ensured. Somalia reaffirms its support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including self-determination, and for a two-State solution with an independent and sovereign Palestine living side by side with Israel in peace and security within recognized borders. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and on this Council to uphold its Charter responsibilities.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We did so because the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is intolerable and because the Council must demand an immediate ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the protection of civilians, and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza.

The United Kingdom unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October 2023, the continued holding of hostages and all acts of hostage-taking. There can be no justification for terrorism. Israel has the right to live in peace and security, but all parties must respect international humanitarian law. The killing of civilians, attacks on schools, hospitals, shelters, UN premises and aid distribution points, and the obstruction of humanitarian relief are unacceptable. Far too many Palestinian civilians, including women and children, have lost their lives, and the risk of famine is real.

We deeply regret that the Council has not been able to adopt this resolution. A veto leaves the Council unable to speak with the clarity the situation demands. We acknowledge the concerns expressed by the United States and share the overriding objective of securing the release of all hostages; but the United Kingdom believes the Council should have been able to send a united message that the fighting must stop, hostages must be released, and aid must flow.

We call on Israel and Hamas to implement resolution 2735 (2024) and to agree and implement the ceasefire proposal without delay and without condition. The hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally. Humanitarian access must be scaled up through all crossings, including to those in need in the north, and humanitarian and UN personnel and premises must be protected.

The United Kingdom rejects any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including forced displacement, and any reduction in Gaza’s territory. We reaffirm our commitment to the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We will continue to work with all partners to end this conflict and build a lasting peace.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr President. The United States has voted against this draft, and we welcome the opportunity to explain why. We deeply regret the humanitarian suffering in Gaza, and we share the urgency of ending this war. But this Council cannot pretend that a resolution can simply will a ceasefire into existence while leaving the hostages in Hamas’s hands. The text before us demanded an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire without making the release of all hostages the essential condition and first step. That is not a path to peace; it is a roadmap to prolonging the war. It would send Hamas a clear message that it can continue to hold innocent people, including American citizens, while the international community relieves the pressure it faces.

The United States has been clear from the outset: any ceasefire must be accompanied by the immediate release of all hostages. We have worked with Egypt, Qatar, Israel and other partners on a practical framework that would bring the hostages home, enable a ceasefire, allow a massive surge of humanitarian assistance, and create the conditions for a durable end to the conflict. The draft did not reflect that reality. It was unbalanced, and it failed to require that Hamas accept the ceasefire and lay down its arms.

Let me also be clear about what this vote does not mean. It does not mean the United States is indifferent to the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. We are not. We continue to press for expanded humanitarian access through all crossings, for the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, and for more aid to reach those in dire need. We call on Israel to do more to protect civilians and facilitate relief, just as we call on Hamas to stop using civilians and civilian infrastructure as shields and to release every hostage immediately.

The Council’s credibility depends on adopting resolutions that are implementable and that squarely address the cause of this war: Hamas’s terrorist attack on 7 October and its continued holding of hostages. The United States remains committed to ending this conflict, bringing all hostages home, and working toward a future of peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike. We urge Hamas to accept the terms on the table and stop delaying. We urge all members of this Council to focus their efforts not on scoring political points, but on the only outcome that can bring real relief: a ceasefire that begins with the release of the hostages.
